model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of iterations and loss across different models. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, with a linear scale, a value range of 0 to 140,000, and tick labels at regular intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents loss, with a linear scale, a value range of 2.4 to 3.4, and tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains six lines, each representing a different model: Vanilla (purple, solid, no marker), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid, no marker), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid, no marker), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid, no marker), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid, no marker), and SepLLM (n=128) (navy blue, solid, no marker). Starting at iteration 0, the loss values are approximately: Vanilla (3.35), StrmLLM (n=64) (3.32), SepLLM (n=64) (3.28), SepLLM (n=64, H) (3.28), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (3.28), and SepLLM (n=128) (3.28). As the number of iterations increases to 140,000, the loss values decrease to approximately: Vanilla (2.49), StrmLLM (n=64) (2.49), SepLLM (n=64) (2.48), SepLLM (n=64, H) (2.48), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (2.48), and SepLLM (n=128) (2.47), with all lines showing a steady decline.
